solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Charlatan after one’s gold rings (8)

indicatorNotes.rings: I'M and OR ring, i.e. surround, the next piece

annotation.surface: A fraudster chases someone's gold jewellery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like it is placing the charlatan after something, but it is wordplay, and 'rings' is a verb, not jewellery.
annotation.definitionFit: An impostor pretends to be someone he is not, which is what a charlatan does.

entries.clue: Not prepared to die crossing river between Iowa and Missouri, say (10)

indicatorNotes.crossing: INTESTATE crosses, i.e. lies across and around, the river letter

blocks.note: intestate = dying without having made a will

annotation.surface: Someone crossing a river is not ready to die.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not prepared to die' is a playful description of INTESTATE: not prepared in the sense of having no will made. Iowa and Missouri are neighbouring US states.
annotation.definitionFit: Interstate means between states, and Iowa and Missouri are two of them.

entries.clue: While taking pictures, rotate roast (3)

blocks.note: a filming term: swinging the camera round horizontally
roast = criticise harshly, as a reviewer does

annotation.surface: A photographer turns a joint of meat on a spit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Roast' suggests cooking, and a pan is kitchenware, but both halves are verbs: roast here means slate a performance.
annotation.definitionFit: Critics pan or roast a bad show; a camera operator pans by rotating the camera.

entries.clue: Short Italian cracks mathematical problem in bed (7)

indicatorNotes.Short: cuts TRATTORIA down to its short form
indicatorNotes.cracks: TRAT cracks SUM, breaking into it

blocks.note: trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant

annotation.surface: An Italian solves a maths problem while lying in bed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Italian' here is a restaurant, not a person; TRAT is the informal short form of trattoria. 'Bed' is the geological sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A stratum is a layer of rock, which geologists also call a bed.

entries.clue: With newspaper and string wrap present unofficially (3,3,6)

indicatorNotes.wrap: FT and CORD wrap around HERE, one either side

blocks.note: of = with, as in 'a man of means'
here = present, as when answering a register

annotation.surface: Someone wraps a gift in newspaper and string.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like the gift being wrapped, but it means attending: HERE, as a pupil answers the register.
annotation.definitionFit: Something said off the record is said unofficially, not for publication.

entries.clue: Curse that fellow with dung in the van (6)

indicatorNotes.in the van: van = vanguard, the front, so SCAT goes first

annotation.surface: Someone swears at a man travelling in a van full of manure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Van' is not a vehicle but the vanguard: dung goes in front of HE.
annotation.definitionFit: To scathe is an old word for to harm or denounce, close to cursing someone.

entries.clue: Eccentric ego exposed lack of heart (7)

indicatorNotes.exposed: LACK exposed has its outer letters stripped away

annotation.surface: An odd person's ego reveals that he is heartless.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'lack of heart' as a phrase, but the definition is 'of heart', so 'lack' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the adjective comes from Greek kardia, heart, as in cardiac arrest.

entries.clue: Hamlet’s first choice — fresh whiting for starters (2,5,4)

indicatorNotes.fresh: WHITING is made fresh, i.e. rearranged

blocks.note: 'To be, or not to be': Hamlet's first option is TO BE

annotation.surface: Hamlet picks fresh whiting as a starter from a menu.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a restaurant order, but 'starters' belongs to the idiom 'for starters', meaning first of all.
annotation.definitionFit: 'To begin with' and 'for starters' both mean firstly.

entries.clue: America’s leader set out the way the world is going (4)

annotation.definition: the way the world is going

indicatorNotes.leader: the leader of America is its first letter
indicatorNotes.out: set out means laid out afresh, so the letters of A and SET are arranged into a new order

annotation.surface: A president lays out where the world is heading.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition sounds political but is literal: the Earth spins towards the east.
annotation.definitionFit: The Earth rotates eastward, so east is the way the world is turning.

entries.clue: English bake after taking everything off, all over island (8)

indicatorNotes.all over: the whole string is turned over, back to front

blocks.note: to fire pottery is to bake it
net = what is left after deductions

annotation.surface: An English sunbather strips off and bakes on an island beach.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a naturist tourist; 'after taking everything off' is NET, as in net pay after tax.
annotation.definitionFit: Tenerife is the largest of the Canary Islands.

entries.clue: Hellish underground before double-decker? (6)

blocks.note: a double-decker is a two-level bus

annotation.surface: A hellish ride on the Tube before a bus journey.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Underground' suggests the London Tube, but it is the Greek underworld. A double-decker is the classic two-storey London bus.
annotation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Erebus is the dark region of the underworld, a hellish place below ground.

entries.clue: Illogical arguments against lives having overarching purpose (12)

indicatorNotes.having overarching: INTENT arches over CONS and IS, holding them inside

annotation.surface: A philosopher dismisses arguments against life having a grand purpose.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Overarching purpose' reads as a philosophical phrase, but 'overarching' is the instruction to put INTENT round the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: Illogical arguments contradict themselves, which is to be inconsistent.

entries.clue: Having conventional opinions is absolutely fine, man (5-8)

blocks.note: a fine thread is a thin one
a king is a chess man

annotation.surface: Someone declares that holding conventional views is perfectly fine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fine' and 'man' both read as casual speech; fine means thin and man is a chess piece.
annotation.definitionFit: Right-thinking people hold the accepted, conventional opinions.

entries.clue: Ill-mannered child threatens to go out and pinch auntie’s bottom (11)

indicatorNotes.bottom: the bottom of a down entry's word is its last letter

blocks.note: a candle gutters when it flickers and threatens to go out

annotation.surface: A rude child threatens to sneak out and pinch his aunt's backside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Threatens' seems to be the child's action, but 'threatens to go out' is one piece: a guttering candle.
annotation.definitionFit: A guttersnipe is a scruffy, badly behaved child of the streets.

entries.clue: Xenophobe on TV dubiously flagrant about alien (3,7)

indicatorNotes.dubiously: FLAGRANT is rearranged, dubiously put together

annotation.surface: A TV bigot is openly rude about foreigners.
annotation.walkthrough: Alf Garnett was the bigoted working-class Londoner in the BBC sitcom Till Death Us Do Part. 'Alien' in the surface means foreigner; in the wordplay it is ET.
annotation.definitionFit: Alf Garnett was a famously xenophobic television character.

entries.clue: Add space on page for emblem (5)

blocks.note: an em is a printer's unit of space

annotation.surface: A designer leaves room on the page for a logo.
annotation.walkthrough: An em is a typesetter's measure of width, originally the width of a capital M.
annotation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem representing a clan or group.

entries.clue: Grub tin Abigail emptied, the way to canine’s heart? (4,5)

indicatorNotes.emptied: Abigail emptied has its middle removed, leaving the outer letters

blocks.note: to grub or root is to dig about for food

annotation.surface: Abigail empties a tin of dog food, since the way to a dog's heart is through its stomach.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface plays on 'the way to a man's heart is through his stomach'; the canine is a tooth, not a dog, and its heart is the pulp.
annotation.definitionFit: A root canal runs through a tooth such as a canine to its pulp, its heart.

entries.clue: Sit and sketch rocky hinterland (3,6)

indicatorNotes.rocky: the letters are shaken up, unsteady

annotation.surface: An artist sits down to draw a rugged landscape.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rocky hinterland' reads as one scenic phrase, but 'rocky' is the anagram instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: The sticks is slang for remote rural country, the hinterland.

entries.clue: Jazz fan raised hat that’s felt (7)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down entry, raising CAT writes it upwards

annotation.surface: A jazz lover lifts his felt hat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Felt' looks like the hat's material, but 'that's felt' is the definition: something perceptible by touch.
annotation.definitionFit: Tactile means perceived by touch, felt.

entries.clue: Charlie and Heather remain in close contact (5)

blocks.note: Charlie = C in the phonetic alphabet
ling is a kind of heather

annotation.surface: Two friends named Charlie and Heather keep in touch.
annotation.walkthrough: Charlie and Heather look like a couple's names; ling is common heather.
annotation.definitionFit: To cling is to stay tightly in contact with something.

entries.clue: King asleep just after a piece of toast (7)

blocks.note: out = unconscious, dead to the world
on = just after, as in 'on arrival'

annotation.surface: A king dozes off straight after eating toast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A piece of toast' reads as what the king ate; it is the definition, a small cube of fried or toasted bread.
annotation.definitionFit: A crouton is a small piece of toasted or fried bread.

entries.clue: Sporting Porsche T-shirt, he gave lifts to one traveller at a time (2,11)

annotation.definition: he gave lifts to one traveller at a time

indicatorNotes.Sporting: the letters are sporting, playing about

annotation.surface: A driver in a Porsche T-shirt gives lifts to hitchhikers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gave lifts' sounds like a car, suiting the Porsche, but the legend has St Christopher carrying travellers across a river on his shoulders, one at a time.
annotation.definitionFit: St Christopher, patron saint of travellers, carried people across a river, including the Christ child.

entries.clue: One to be avoided by biker when cycling? (4)

annotation.definition: One to be avoided by biker when cycling?

indicatorNotes.avoided by: BIKER avoids ONE, dropping the I
indicatorNotes.cycling: the first letter cycles round to the end

blocks.note: B moves from front to back

annotation.surface: A question about a hazard a cyclist steers clear of.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: cyclists avoid the kerb, the raised edge of the pavement (US curb).
annotation.definitionFit: A kerb is the pavement edge that a cyclist must avoid hitting.

entries.clue: Evoke boundless happiness (6)

indicatorNotes.boundless: FELICITY loses its bounds, the first and last letters

blocks.note: felicity = happiness, minus F and Y

annotation.surface: Something that brings out unlimited joy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boundless' looks like a description of the happiness, but it removes the bounding letters of FELICITY.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to draw out a reaction or memory from someone.

entries.clue: Star to write chapter in story (8)

indicatorNotes.in: chapter in story means the chapter sits inside the story, so C is placed within TALE

annotation.surface: A celebrity is set to write a chapter of a novel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a celebrity; it is the five-pointed figure.
annotation.definitionFit: A pentacle is a five-pointed star, used as a magic symbol.

entries.clue: Softly murmur how lovely that is (3)

blocks.note: the soft sound a dove or pigeon makes
a dated British exclamation of delight or surprise

annotation.surface: Someone murmurs quietly in admiration.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coo!' is a dated British exclamation of wonder, like 'gosh', and doves coo.
annotation.definitionFit: A dove coos softly, and 'coo!' expresses delight.

entries.clue: Eg queen with a bellyful had a bellyache (6)

blocks.note: a queen bee is one kind of bee

annotation.surface: A monarch overeats and then gets a stomach ache.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bellyache' is slang for complain, not a pain, and 'queen' is a bee.
annotation.definitionFit: To beef and to bellyache are both slang for complaining.

entries.clue: Excellent case of Sekt, Cockney’s charitable donation (8)

indicatorNotes.case of: the case of Sekt is its outer letters
indicatorNotes.Cockney’s: Cockneys drop their Hs, so HANDOUT loses its H

annotation.surface: A Londoner gives away a case of German sparkling wine to charity.
annotation.walkthrough: Sekt is German sparkling wine. Cockney speech drops the H, so a handout becomes 'andout.
annotation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, it describes something that stands out from the rest because it is so good.
